document.title: Security audit 2026-11-07 (18): rename from obs-nixie-countdown to nixie-countdown

acknowledgments.summary: audit of pull request rename/nixie-countdown before merge, directed by the maintainer

notes.title: Summary
notes.text: Audit of the rename required by the OBS Project's plugin guidelines (no 'OBS' in resource names): the repository (now simulacra10/nixie-countdown; GitHub redirects the old URL), the module and file names, the macOS bundle ID, the Debian package and the source headers. Earlier security logs keep the old name and URLs as historical records; the old URLs redirect. No security issues found.

notes.title: Audit details
notes.text: Download scripts (run-tests.ps1, run-tests.sh) now use the new repository name for the GitHub API and archive URLs and the new archive folder name; the trusted-commit check (NIXIE-2026-006) is unchanged and runs against the same repository under its new name. dev-install.sh removes only the fixed folder ~/.config/obs-studio/plugins/obs-nixie-countdown after installing the renamed plugin. The verification scripts now fail if the old plugin is still installed, because OBS would load both and they register the same source type; they only check for the old paths and never delete them. The Debian package declares Conflicts and Replaces on obs-nixie-countdown so apt removes the old package. The source type ID nixie_countdown_source is unchanged, so existing scenes keep working.

notes.title: Test evidence
notes.text: On Debian 13 with OBS 30.2.3: clean build produces nixie-countdown.so; dev-install.sh installed it and removed the old obs-nixie-countdown folder; unit tests pass (101 checks). verify-linux-macos.py against a separate OBS config: with an old plugin folder present the new check fails and names the folder; without it all 23 automated checks pass and OBS loads the plugin under its new name.

notes.title: Result
notes.text: No findings. Logged as required by the project's audit policy.
